**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/24 (Wed) 00:13
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Part One discussed income, capital and growth since the Industrial Revolution.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Part Two focuses on capital stock, its overall size and its breakdown into different types of assets.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Different forms of wealth will be examined over time, starting with Britain and France.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Literature from the nineteenth century offers a good introduction to the subject of wealth.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Wealth was understood to exist to produce rents, or dependable payments to asset owners.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Land and government bonds were the most common forms of wealth in the nineteenth century.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The characters in nineteenth-century novels seem like archetypes of the rentier, a suspect figure in the modern era.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The differences between the nineteenth and twenty-first centuries are less apparent than they might seem.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Government bonds should be excluded from national wealth and included solely in private wealth.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The complex question of government debt and wealth associated with it is still important today.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Financial intermediation has become so complex that people are often unaware of who owns what.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Many forms of capital played an essential role not only in classic novels but in the society of the time.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Père Goriot made his fortune as a pasta manufacturer and grain merchant.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Goriot sold his share of the business and invested in perpetual government bonds.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] César Birotteau made his money in perfumes.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Birotteau was the ingenious inventor of any number of beauty products.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] A perfect capital market produces a reliable and steady income.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Today’s public debt is at or near a historical record in France and many other countries.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The process of financial intermediation is more complex today than it was in the past.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The mystery of who owns what needs to be dispelled, and studying the past can help us do so.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Classic novels show the importance of the development of new technologies and distribution networks.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Goriot's capital gains were similar to those of a twenty-first-century startup founder.
